6.4.2 Criterion for Row-Sparse and Low-Rank Matrices
We now consider the case where the matrix A
∗
has a low rank and a small number of
nonzero rows. The rank of a matrix is not larger than the number of its nonzero rows,
so the estimator (6.19) already has a small rank. But here we have in mind a case
where the rank of A
∗
is much smaller than the number of its nonzero rows, and we
want to exploit this feature. The rank of A
∗
and the location of its nonzero rows are
unknown. We first investigate how much we can gain by taking into account simulta-
neously row sparsity and low rank. In this direction, a model selection estimator will
be our benchmark.
